srs_summary.product_purpose: Hardware-light in-store product discovery and navigation that connects store-managed catalog/freshness data with published walking graphs, shopping lists and pickup reservations, targeting at least 40% lower median product-finding time.
primary_users: Customer / Shopper (mobile; guest discovery is Should)
Store Owner / Manager (web, owned or assigned stores)
Store Staff / Data Operator (web, explicit store permissions)
Product Owner and Pilot Store Management (acceptance and KPI stakeholders)
primary_business_flows: Manager submits store application -> PENDING_APPROVAL -> administrator approves to ACTIVE or rejects to REJECTED; ACTIVE may be suspended and reactivated with audit and owner notification.
Manager provisions assigned staff -> operator maintains categories-backed catalog or uploads CSV/XLSX -> validation preview -> explicit confirm -> transactional matched upserts with per-row outcomes.

Operator uploads floor plan -> edits hierarchy/nodes/edges -> validates route preview -> publishes atomic map version -> assigns product locations -> verifies price/stock/location data; closures update the graph revision.

Customer selects active store or resolves checkpoint QR -> searches/browses -> opens product detail/freshness/location -> selects known start -> sees mapped walking route or an explicit unavailable reason.

Authenticated customer maintains per-store list -> route service skips unavailable/unmapped items with reasons -> orders valid destinations -> collected-state updates recalculate the remaining path under the approved start policy.

Customer reviews a same-store cart -> server validates availability and atomically creates an idempotent SUBMITTED reservation -> store notification -> ACCEPTED -> PREPARING -> READY_FOR_PICKUP -> COMPLETED; approved REJECTED/CANCELLED/EXPIRED guards are pending GAP-017.

Customer reports location/price/availability issue -> OPEN -> IN_REVIEW -> RESOLVED or DISMISSED -> explicit authorized correction/verification updates customer-visible data and records resolver/audit history.

Platform admin governs accounts, categories, limits and audit review -> operations monitor health/failures and rehearse restore -> pilot staff compare measured find-time/location/freshness/usability results to acceptance thresholds.
core_entities: User: own profile, contact/verification, role/status; sensitive data accessible only for permitted purposes.
Store: owner, public metadata, operating status/hours/timezone and freshness settings.
StoreUser: explicit user/store assignment, role/permissions and active status; unique membership.
Category: governed hierarchical classification with status and protected references.

Product: optional shared descriptive identity; StoreProduct: store-owned SKU/barcode/name/description/image references, decimal price, stock/status, optional quantity and independent update/verification timestamps.
ProductLocation: StoreProduct-linked zone/aisle/rack/shelf, map target and verification provenance; spatial hierarchy is store-scoped.
StoreMap: store/version/image/dimensions/active flag; MapNode: type/label/coordinates/active; MapEdge: endpoints/weight/accessibility/active/closure flags; one atomic active map revision.
ShoppingList and derived ShoppingListItem: customer/store-owned products and collection state; distinct from a reservation cart.
Reservation and ReservationItem: one customer/store, status/history/totals/notes/timestamps and immutable submission snapshots; derived idempotency ledger and stock holds follow approved policy.
DataIssueReport: customer/product/store/issue/note/status/resolution/resolver; append resolution history as a necessary audit detail.
ImportJob and derived ImportRowResult: scoped file metadata/validation/version/progress/counts/errors and resumable commit outcomes.
Notification and derived OutboxEvent: recipient/type/minimal payload/delivery/read state and deduplicated post-commit dispatch.
AuditLog: actor/action/entity/redacted before-after reference/time/context with append-only application writes.
Derived technical records: refresh sessions, verification/reset challenges, approved configuration keys and privacy-minimized analytics events; essential enablers, not additional business products.
major_constraints: Source is a proposed v2.0 baseline, not evidence that open business policies are approved.
Exactly three developers and three target Trello lists. Each feature has three platform cards; application surface scope follows the SRS.
All requested target dates lie between 2026-09-10 and 2026-10-24. The full scope is NOT resource-feasible in this window; GAP-001 quantifies the overload.

Planning technology override (2026-09-11): Flutter customer app; HTML5/JavaScript/CSS3/Tailwind CSS operational web; .NET Core Web API and FastAPI backend split approximately 60%/40% by planned backend effort; PostgreSQL, durable object storage and configured notifications remain.
Online operation, manually maintained catalog/maps and hardware-light checkpoint navigation; no implied continuous indoor localization.
No online card payments, digital wallets, delivery/driver tracking, required beacons, mandatory AI/image search, automatic map generation, deep POS/ERP, dynamic pricing or loyalty.
Typed SKU/barcode search is in scope; camera product barcode lookup is future scope, distinct from required store/checkpoint QR scanning.
Future POS/ERP/payment/loyalty/promotions/AI/BLE/heatmap items are traced as exclusion/compatibility constraints, not scheduled implementation.
Must requirements are retained; Should requirements remain visible; FR-021 Could is optional/disabled pending decision and counted as mapped, not delivered.
Pilot store catalog/layout, provider credentials, infrastructure access, privacy decisions and test participants are external dependencies.
No Trello boards/lists/cards are created by this deliverable. It is an import-ready planning document; an importing agent resolves actual board/list/label IDs and preserves canonical identifiers.
key_non_functional_requirements: Search, product detail/map metadata and normal route API p95 <=2 seconds under agreed pilot load/graph definitions.
Monthly pilot availability >=99.5% excluding announced maintenance; measurement requires the relevant observation period.
Transactional critical writes and idempotent reservation creation, tenant-scoped server authorization, adaptive password hashing, expiring/revocable sessions and rate-limited authentication.
HTTPS, validated safe uploads, redacted audit history/logs, secrets outside source control and purpose-limited personal-data access.
Daily database backups; MVP RPO <=24 hours and RTO <=4 hours; <=1 hour RPO/PITR is a recommended production goal where supported.
Stateless horizontally scalable API, indexed access, domain modularity and automated critical unit/API/system tests.
At least 80% independent task completion and no more than four primary actions from selected store to normal named-product route display.
Applicable WCAG 2.2 AA controls, approved Android/iOS and stable Chrome/Edge/Firefox compatibility matrix, and externalized text resources.
Structured errors/logs, health/readiness, p50/p95/p99 endpoint metrics and import/notification/reservation/backup failure monitoring.

Pilot gates: >=1000 realistic products; one complete published map; >=95% physical location accuracy; >=90% data freshness; >=40% median locate-time improvement; <=15-minute trained-operator upload/validation excluding data preparation.

requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 8.2; 2.3; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Money and quantity integrity
requirements.summary: Prices must be non-negative decimal-compatible values; maintained quantities must be non-negative.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 8.2; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Map bounds and reference integrity
requirements.summary: Validate map coordinates against bounds and category/location/node references before commit.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 8.2; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Import transaction strategy
requirements.summary: Invalid rows must not partially overwrite valid existing records unless an explicit transactional strategy is defined.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 8.2; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Reservation snapshots
requirements.summary: Preserve item snapshot information sufficient to reconstruct the submitted reservation.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 8.2; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Import columns and navigation readiness
requirements.summary: Support store_sku, optional barcode, product_name, category, price, stock_status, optional quantity, zone, aisle, rack, shelf, map_target. Zone/aisle are required for navigation, map_target for routes, rack/shelf recommended.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 8.3; Appendix B; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Core state models
requirements.summary: Use store, reservation, report and import states from Appendix C; resolve unspecified terminal-transition guards explicitly.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); Appendix C; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Expiring and revocable sessions
requirements.summary: Use token authentication with secure expiration/refresh appropriate to mobile and web.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 12 Authentication; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Recovery token safety
requirements.summary: Password reset tokens must be single-use and time-limited.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 12 Password Security; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Input and upload security
requirements.summary: Validate API schemas; restrict upload extensions, MIME types and sizes; use generated names and non-executable storage paths.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 12 Input Validation; Upload Security; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Abuse protection
requirements.summary: Apply rate limits to login, recovery, verification and other abuse-sensitive endpoints.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 12 Rate Limiting; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Secrets management
requirements.summary: Store secrets in environment/secret manager and never hard-code them in source control.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 12 Secrets; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Privacy policy and deletion decisions
requirements.summary: Finalize retention, deletion workflow and jurisdiction-specific privacy requirements before production deployment.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 12 Privacy; 5.3; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Supported platform boundaries
requirements.summary: Planning override (2026-09-11): Flutter customer app on Android/iOS; store/admin web using HTML5, JavaScript, CSS3 and Tailwind CSS; backend split between .NET Core Web API (~60%) and FastAPI (~40%); PostgreSQL recommended; object storage and configured push/email notifications.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 3.1; 5.1; 11.1-11.2; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Versioned REST and OpenAPI
requirements.summary: Use versioned REST JSON APIs over HTTPS with OpenAPI documentation generated by .NET Core Web API and FastAPI; version breaking changes or apply a controlled compatibility strategy.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 11.3; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Online operation and hardware-light routing
requirements.summary: Normal operation assumes internet; optional recently viewed map caching; no specialized indoor-positioning hardware required. Routing depends on maintained graph/location data.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 2.3; 5.3; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Environment separation
requirements.summary: Provide development, production-like staging and controlled production/pilot environments.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 14.1; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Durable deployment storage
requirements.summary: Managed API/web hosting is allowed; prefer managed PostgreSQL; store product/map images in object storage, not ephemeral server disk.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 14.2; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Operational monitoring
requirements.summary: Monitor API errors/health, p50/p95/p99 latency, DB health, import failures, notification failures, reservation errors, unresolved reports and backup failures.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 14.3; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Operational ownership
requirements.summary: Assign platform incident/backup/security responsibility, manager accuracy/permission responsibility, staff data upkeep, and product-owner release/KPI acceptance.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 14.4; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Critical automated test layers
requirements.summary: Unit tests for routing, imports, authorization and reservation states; API integration tests for auth/scoping/catalog/maps/reservations/admin; system tests across app/dashboard/API/database.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 13.1; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Security and performance validation
requirements.summary: Test authorization bypass, unsafe uploads, session handling and common web/API vulnerabilities; benchmark agreed pilot load.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 13.1; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Usability and pilot UAT
requirements.summary: Run real/representative-store usability testing and customer/staff acceptance sessions.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 13.1; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Pilot measurement definitions
requirements.summary: Measure find time median/distribution vs manual baseline, physical location accuracy, correct-search success, no-result rate, freshness, independent task completion, reservation terminal completion and time-to-response.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 13.3; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Original roadmap and 45-day override
requirements.summary: Source phases span nine weeks including validation and pilot hardening. The attached task overrides the deadline with 45 calendar days and three developers, one per stream; feasibility must be assessed rather than presumed.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 15; attached task PROJECT CONTEXT; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Pilot inputs and baseline readiness
requirements.summary: Participating stores supply catalog/layout; phase 0 includes interviews, sample catalog/map format and manual-find benchmark.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 5.3; 15 Phase 0; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Excluded MVP capabilities
requirements.summary: No card payment/digital wallets, dispatch/driver tracking, centimeter positioning, required beacons, mandatory AI image search, automatic map generation, deep POS/ERP, dynamic pricing, loyalty or extra languages beyond the chosen MVP language(s).
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 3.2; analyst-assigned ID

requirements.title: Future integration compatibility
requirements.summary: Keep future POS/ERP, payment, delivery, camera barcode lookup, AI semantic/substitution, labeled promotions, loyalty and BLE/Wi-Fi/heatmap options architecturally possible; do not implement them in this 45-day baseline.
requirements.source_reference: DAWER SRS v2.0 (proposed baseline, 2026-09-10); 3.3; 11.4; 15.1; analyst-assigned ID

srs_gaps.topic: Full-scope capacity does not fit the requested deadline
srs_gaps.description: The source roadmap spans nine weeks. Requested dates span 45 calendar days, 32 Monday-Friday weekdays, with one developer per platform. Bottom-up estimates are FE 63.5, BE 99, Mobile 54.25 developer-days. Even assuming all 45 calendar days are worked, each stream exceeds capacity. At 80% planning utilization, usable capacity is 25.6 days per stream. Dates below are requested targets, not a feasible committed schedule. Mapping 100% of the SRS does not mean 100% can be delivered in this window.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 1, the product owner must choose a smaller vertical pilot with explicitly revised requirements, increase staffing, or extend the deadline. Preserve the full backlog and traceability in all cases. Do not hide overload by overlapping work assigned to the same developer, shrinking estimates, or silently dropping Must requirements. Even deferring F-030 alone is insufficient. With unchanged scope and 80% utilization, backend effort alone needs at least 124 weekdays before dependency/calendar effects. Requested 45-day targets must remain labeled UNCOMMITTED until replanning is accepted.

srs_gaps.topic: Three cards versus actual product platform scope
srs_gaps.description: The task requires FE/BE/Mobile cards for every feature, but the SRS defines customer mobile and staff/admin web. Building every screen three times would introduce unsupported customer-web and mobile-admin products.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Use exactly three cards per feature as requested, with customer-only FE work limited to relevant operational preview/shared-contract verification and staff-only Mobile work limited to downstream customer behavior. Fractional estimates represent this limited effort. If full UI parity is intended, revise the SRS and re-estimate before commitment.

srs_gaps.topic: Identity channel, verification and session policy
srs_gaps.description: The SRS permits email or mobile registration but does not select verification/recovery provider, contact normalization, password policy, verification expiry/resend limits, guest-to-user handling, web token storage or profile contact-change rules.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 2 select a verified contact channel and provider; document normalization and password rules, one-use challenge expiry, resend/attempt limits, permitted profile fields, contact reverification and reset-session revocation. Proposed design uses short-lived access tokens with revocable rotating refresh sessions, secure mobile storage and a reviewed web cookie/CSRF strategy. Numeric values remain unapproved configuration, not invented SRS requirements.

srs_gaps.topic: Manager provisioning, staff permissions and bootstrap
srs_gaps.description: Store manager submission and staff invitation/creation are required, but first manager creation, role grants, permission presets, invitation expiry, last-manager removal and initial administrator bootstrap are undefined.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 2 define trusted manager onboarding and secure first-admin provisioning, a concrete permission matrix for catalog/map/reservation/report/settings/staff actions, invite versus direct creation, expiry and last-manager/self-lockout protections. Prohibit self-assigned platform privileges.

srs_gaps.topic: Store hours, selection and guest context
srs_gaps.description: Opening status lacks timezone/overnight/holiday definitions. Guest browsing and most-recent-store memory are Should requirements; store switching with existing lists/carts is unspecified.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 define store timezone and overnight interval encoding; use ordinary weekly hours unless pilot requirements explicitly add holidays. Permit guest discovery as planned, gate persistent lists/reservations, revalidate last store and confirm clearing/replacing a different-store cart without mixing items.

srs_gaps.topic: Reference deactivation and historical retention
srs_gaps.description: Soft-delete is preferred but behavior for categories with active products, location hierarchy with mapped items, users with reservations and rejected-store resubmission is not fully specified.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Before affected CRUD is finalized, define per-entity deactivation/cascade restrictions. Preserve reservation snapshots/audit history, reject destructive changes to active referenced nodes, and require explicit product/category reassignment or a documented deactivation policy. Rejected stores remain terminal unless a new application policy is approved.

srs_gaps.topic: Store product identity and match normalization
srs_gaps.description: The matching rule is configurable but no concrete rule is selected. Barcode is explicitly not globally unique; SKU normalization, case sensitivity, shared Product ownership and matching conflicts are unclear.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 2 approve (store_id, normalized store_sku) as the MVP unique key, preserve leading zeros, define case/whitespace rules and keep barcode nonunique unless locally constrained. Document precedence for file-internal duplicates and shared descriptive-data ownership. Do not merge products merely because barcodes match.

srs_gaps.topic: Bulk import commit semantics
srs_gaps.description: The SRS demands validation-before-commit, valid-row processing and COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS while warning against partial overwrites unless a transaction strategy is explicit. No job atomicity, resume or stale-preview policy is selected.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 approve per-row atomic upserts for valid rows with invalid rows skipped and counted; no partial field update within a rejected row. Require explicit confirm, validation fingerprint/version, revalidation at commit and durable progress/idempotency. If all-or-nothing jobs are chosen instead, revise both clients, tests and COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS semantics together.

srs_gaps.topic: Minimum location completeness and coordinate destinations
srs_gaps.description: FR-022 suggests all Zone/Aisle/Rack/Shelf fields, while the import template recommends rack/shelf and conditionally requires map_target. It allows a node or coordinate without defining snapping to walkable paths.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 define navigation-ready versus catalog-only products. Proposed baseline requires valid zone/aisle and a reachable target, with optional rack/shelf displayed only when known. Normalize coordinate destinations to validated graph attachment nodes using an explicitly approved snapping rule; otherwise require an operator-selected node. Never route to an arbitrary unconnected coordinate.

srs_gaps.topic: Map graph semantics and publication lifecycle
srs_gaps.description: Graph units, directed versus bidirectional edges, image scaling, accessibility flags, connectivity publication blockers, version replacement and closures during active routes are undefined.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 agree coordinate origin/units, map bounds, edge directionality, valid weights and calibration. Use relative length until a meter scale is verified. Publish immutable image/graph revisions atomically, preserve draft isolation, define disconnected destination handling, and invalidate old routes on graph changes. Accessibility flags do not automatically imply a new accessible-route product mode without scope approval.

srs_gaps.topic: QR creation and checkpoint persistence
srs_gaps.description: QR scanning is required but producing/distributing codes, payload schema, node-less codes, retired checkpoint behavior and map-version compatibility are not specified.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 approve a versioned store/checkpoint identifier payload resolved by the server, printable/downloadable operator QR controls as a necessary enabler, safe node-less manual start selection and explicit invalid/retired responses. Define whether checkpoint IDs are stable across publications; reject arbitrary untrusted URLs/coordinates.

srs_gaps.topic: Search language, ranking and aliases
srs_gaps.description: Exact and in-stock ranking priorities can conflict. Supported spelling variants, aliases/keywords editing, search language, stable sort and empty-query behavior are undefined.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 approve a query test set and deterministic ranking: proposed exact identifier/name tier first, then match quality with in-stock preference within comparable tiers, then stable ID tie break. Confirm MVP language normalization and bounded alias matching; no AI dependency. Keep typed identifier lookup distinct from deferred camera barcode scanning.

srs_gaps.topic: List quantity and concurrency semantics
srs_gaps.description: Persistent lists do not specify one or several lists per store, quantities, duplicate additions, collected-state persistence or multi-device conflict rules.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 4 choose one active persistent list per customer/store for the baseline, define duplicate-add behavior and collected-state persistence, and use versioned mutations. Additional named/shared lists are outside this plan unless explicitly approved. Keep cart quantity independent from any optional list quantity.

srs_gaps.topic: Multi-stop optimization and changing start position
srs_gaps.description: Optimized visit order lacks a quality target, maximum list size, performance bound, unreachable-item policy and the current start to use after marking items collected. Hardware-light routing cannot infer precise continuous customer position.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Before F-019 implementation, approve a bounded deterministic heuristic, representative benchmark lists and maximum destinations. Require no worse length than original visit order on agreed fixtures. Deduplicate nodes, explicitly skip unavailable/unmapped/unreachable items, and use a confirmed checkpoint/manual start or approved collected-node assumption. Never claim globally optimal or live-position accuracy.

srs_gaps.topic: Availability, inventory holds and suspended-store operations
srs_gaps.description: Stock may be status-only or include quantity. Deduction/hold timing, hold release, status-versus-quantity precedence, quantity cap, oversell behavior and open reservations when a store is suspended are undefined.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 select whether submission atomically places holds or requests manual confirmation, define stock-status/quantity precedence and status-only quantity limits, then define release at rejection/cancellation/expiry/completion. Transactional conditional updates must prevent negative maintained quantity. Separately specify how existing reservations are served after store suspension; do not silently cancel them.

srs_gaps.topic: Reservation amounts, currency and changed prices
srs_gaps.description: Price is decimal-compatible but currency, scale, quantity unit, tax treatment, displayed total and price changes between cart review and submission are unspecified.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 choose store currency and decimal precision/rounding plus quantity units. Preserve item name/SKU/price/currency/quantity snapshots at submission. Require review of changed prices before a new submission intent. Do not add payment collection, tax-engine or receipt functionality not specified by the SRS.

srs_gaps.topic: Reservation terminal transitions, cancellation and expiry
srs_gaps.description: Appendix C lists terminal states but not which nonterminal states allow rejection/cancellation/expiry, who can trigger them, cutoff interpretation, expiry duration, reopening or required reasons.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Before lifecycle implementation, approve a complete actor/state transition matrix. Proposed normal path follows Appendix C with no terminal reopening, rejection from SUBMITTED, customer cancellation only before the configured cutoff, and expiry driven by an approved store duration/status policy. Define scheduler timezone, hold-release and reason/notes rules; test every permitted and forbidden edge.

srs_gaps.topic: Notification channels, recipients and delivery guarantees
srs_gaps.description: The architecture mentions configured push/email providers, while the future roadmap lists messaging integrations. The MVP event channels, store recipients, fallback, token lifecycle and retry limits are not chosen.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 2 select the minimum MVP provider/channel set for required reservation and onboarding notifications; broader messaging integrations remain future. Define authorized store recipients, in-app persistence/read state, safe lock-screen payloads, retry/dead-letter handling and denied-push fallback. Use transactional outbox and event deduplication; obtain provider credentials before integration dates.

srs_gaps.topic: Reporting access, moderation and resolution details
srs_gaps.description: Guest reporting is not explicitly allowed or denied. Note limits, duplicate/abuse policy, report visibility, resolution reasons and direct OPEN-to-terminal actions are not specified.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Approve authenticated reporting for baseline unless guest access is explicitly selected, bounded plain-text notes and retry deduplication. Use OPEN to IN_REVIEW to RESOLVED/DISMISSED from Appendix C; define whether resolution reasons are required. Staff correction stays an explicit separate authorized action. Do not add customer report-history screens without scope.

srs_gaps.topic: Could alternatives versus future AI substitution
srs_gaps.description: FR-021 is optional Could, while semantic search/substitution is future scope. A concrete alternative-selection rule and source of equivalence are absent.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Keep F-030 disabled and its tasks optional. If approved, use manually configured same-store links or another explicit simple rule with no equivalence guarantee and no automatic replacements. No AI substitution engine is included. This full backlog maps the option but does not represent approval or delivery of it.

srs_gaps.topic: Pilot event definitions and measurement protocol
srs_gaps.description: Targets exist but sample size, query set, participant selection, comparable manual baseline, task start/end, event deduplication, timezone windows and reporting retention are undefined.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 2 agree participant/task/store samples, baseline method and objective observation of arrival. Define analytics event IDs, counts/cohorts, query privacy, time-to-response and freshness denominators; document excluded/missing observations. Collect the manual baseline before intervention and require measured results rather than estimating target achievement from software completion.

srs_gaps.topic: Platform settings and freshness defaults
srs_gaps.description: FR-081 names selected limits without listing allowed keys, ranges, precedence, defaults or behavior when changing platform bounds conflicts with store settings.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 define an allowlist of typed configuration keys, data-type freshness defaults/min/max and how effective values resolve. Reject invalid overrides and explicitly migrate or flag conflicting store values when bounds change. Do not invent arbitrary configurable business rules.

srs_gaps.topic: Supported devices, browsers, languages and accessibility scope
srs_gaps.description: Current Android/iOS versions and selected MVP languages are not enumerated. Applicable WCAG controls and the source four-action journey need a repeatable test interpretation.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 2 approve a specific device/OS and stable Chrome/Edge/Firefox test matrix plus language(s), RTL requirements if selected and externalized resources. Count search entry, result selection and navigate actions from an already selected store without hiding required steps. Evaluate applicable WCAG 2.2 AA controls, including text alternatives for map content.

srs_gaps.topic: Hosting, object storage and distribution dependencies
srs_gaps.description: Hosting/vendor region, object-storage policies, worker support, domain/TLS, backup retention, alert owners, signing credentials and iOS/Android pilot distribution are unspecified.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 2 choose pilot infrastructure and distribution route and provide access/credentials. Validate durable worker execution and shared session/rate-limit state across replicas. Define daily backup retention and restore asset dependencies; assign alert recipients and reserve signing/distribution lead time. Do not assume free hosting or instant app-store approval.

srs_gaps.topic: Audit event completeness and access policy
srs_gaps.description: The source requires before/after references, actors and context, but exact critical fields, retention, redaction, immutability privileges and audit time range limits are not defined.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 3 define audited actions and redacted before/after references, actor/session correlation, UTC timestamps and permitted query ranges. Make application audit writes append-only, restrict administrator reads by purpose, and reconcile retention with the approved privacy/history policy. Never log passwords, reset codes or bearer tokens.

srs_gaps.topic: Deployment jurisdiction and personal-data lifecycle
srs_gaps.description: The SRS explicitly defers jurisdiction-specific privacy, retention and deletion workflow decisions. Requirements cannot be finalized from this document alone.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Product owner must identify deployment jurisdiction and obtain the appropriate policy decision before production. Record purposes, permitted roles, retention periods, deletion/anonymization treatment for history/backups and any required disclosure/consent/access workflows. Implement only the approved policy and do not claim legal compliance from this analysis.

srs_gaps.topic: Freshness verification and stale availability behavior
srs_gaps.description: The source requires update/verification times but does not define never-verified status, clock authority, how price/stock/location freshness combines, or whether stale stock blocks reservations.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Approve server UTC as authoritative and per-type effective time as the latest valid update or verification. Treat missing timestamps as unknown, preserve independent data-type values and document the all-required-types denominator for OBJ-03. Display staleness; reserve-blocking due solely to age needs a separate explicit decision rather than an invented rule.

srs_gaps.topic: Pilot load, graph size and benchmark definition
srs_gaps.description: Two-second p95 targets depend on agreed load and normal graphs, but concurrency, dataset size per store, graph size, list size, caching state, network inclusion and benchmark duration are unspecified.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: By day 2 define requests/sec and concurrency, representative catalog/graph/list sizes, benchmark duration and warm/cold scenarios. Measure API p95 separately from mobile user-perceived latency. Apply the normal-route target to the approved workload; explicitly settle whether optimized multi-stop routes share the same bound.

srs_gaps.topic: Optional pickup wording versus mandatory requirements
srs_gaps.description: Product summary calls reservation optional, but sections 3.1 and 6.6/6.9 plus AC-09 require reservation and notification lifecycle for the pilot.
srs_gaps.recommended_resolution: Treat pickup as an optional customer action but a required system capability in this backlog. Removing it to meet 45 days is a formal scope revision affecting the Must requirements and pilot acceptance; do not silently classify it as a dispensable enhancement.

Cross-feature verification/operations/pilot work is separately allocated in F-027 through F-029. Estimates are independent of the allowed target date and must not be silently reduced to meet it.

CAPACITY_BASELINE: 45 calendar days contain 32 Monday-Friday workdays; no holidays or leave are assumed because none were supplied. At 80% utilization, capacity is 25.6 developer-days per stream. Full-scope overload is FE 37.9, BE 73.4, Mobile 28.65 days. Zero-buffer weekday overload remains FE 31.5, BE 67, Mobile 22.25 days.

CAPACITY_SCENARIOS: even working all 45 days without breaks leaves FE 18.5, BE 54, Mobile 9.25 days of overload. At the 80% weekday baseline, aggregate effort divided by capacity gives lower bounds of 3 frontend, 4 backend and 3 mobile developers, before dependency, onboarding and indivisible-work effects; this is not a staffing recommendation or a guarantee of 45-day feasibility.

UNCHANGED_TEAM_SCENARIO: backend 99/0.8 requires at least 124 weekdays, about 24.8 workweeks, before dependency effects; this is a lower bound, not an approved extended due date. All card dates remain within the requested window solely as targets.

Original SRS nine-week roadmap is contextual planning information, not evidence that nine weeks is sufficient. The attached 45-day instruction takes precedence for requested target dates; feasibility analysis takes precedence over unsupported claims of success.

No Should/Must requirement is silently deferred. FR-021 is the only separately conditional Could feature. Any schedule-driven scope reduction must update the requirement baseline, acceptance gates and coverage disposition explicitly.

Canonical complexity follows the largest platform estimate: XS <=2, S <=4, M <=7 and L <=10 developer-days. Fractional effort below one day is limited cross-platform integration/verification, not a separate full implementation. No feature exceeds the source 7-10-day size guidance.

Feature dependencies are completion prerequisites. Early API contracts/mocks enable development before a dependency is complete; this does not remove final integration dependencies or imply a developer can perform concurrent full-day tasks. Same-day dependent targets require the prerequisite integration first.

Contract kickoff occurs on day 1 for identity, store/product IDs, money/timestamps, error/state semantics, graph revision and reservation idempotency. Feature-specific OpenAPI details are agreed at each feature start; later breaking changes are versioned.

Platform responsibility is intentionally asymmetric: admin/catalog/map maintenance screens belong to web; shopper search/map/list/reservation screens belong to Flutter. Opposite-platform cards contain only relevant contract, preview or downstream integration checks, satisfying the requested three-card format without inventing UI parity.

Proposed REST paths, response schemas, optimistic versions, outbox/session/import-row records and implementation algorithms are engineering recommendations derived from required behavior; they are not verbatim source requirements or pre-existing APIs.

Unspecified business decisions remain explicit in srs_gaps. Tasks that depend on a policy must use the approved resolution before implementation. Suggested defaults are provisional, not user authorization for an external action.

Normal operations require connectivity. No durable offline mutation queue or real-time indoor position tracking is added. Optional map caching is versioned and cannot justify accepting stale stock or routes.

Pilot discovery/interviews, catalog/layout collection, manual-find baseline and participant scheduling begin on day 1 within F-029, although final acceptance is due day 45. Infrastructure setup and security decisions start in F-001/individual features; F-027/F-028 are final verification gates, not the first security or deployment work.

Best-effort sequence targets a complete integrated find/list/reservation/report journey by day 37, followed by metrics and stabilization. This target is not capacity-backed under the unchanged team; GAP-001 must be resolved before it is committed.

Coverage means traceability of all identified normative requirements, source use cases, measurable objectives, acceptance gates and material unnumbered constraints. It is not implementation completion, business-policy resolution, test success or approval of a Could feature.

Existing source identifiers FR-001..FR-081, BR-01..BR-15, NFR-01..NFR-24, OBJ-01..OBJ-08, UC-01..UC-08 and AC-01..AC-10 are preserved. Analyst-assigned DR/SEC/ARC/OPS/QA/PLAN/SCOPE IDs capture material unnumbered requirements. Document credits, definitions and future marketing vision are not invented product features.

Trello import must preserve feature/platform title prefixes as stable identities, use only the three requested TODO lists, create checklist items as incomplete and resolve due dates in a chosen board timezone without day shifting. If re-importing, inspect canonical IDs and existing cards before mutation to avoid duplicates. No actual external write is performed here.
